turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you here today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I'm here because my left hand, kind of just like at the base of my thumb, has been hurting for the past two days and it seems to be getting worse, um and I'm left handed so it's really hard for me to write or do anything um where I have to like, clench or grip things.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long has this been going on for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, so for the past two days, but it's got, it got bad yesterday.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any, uh if you were to describe the pain, where is it located exactly?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's just at the base of my thumb. Uh you know where the fleshy part of your hand is?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah yeah.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so just just over there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what kind of pain is it? Is it sharp or is it aching?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, it's it's like a um, at baseline it's an achy pain, but if I try to move it or um try to write or you know, use a computer or anything like that, it becomes sharp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, Um and on a scale of uh zero to 10, 10 being the worst pain you've felt in your life, how much would you rate it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'd say like a 6.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does this pain move anywhere else in your hand, or does it just stay where you described?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um it just stays there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what kind of motions uh cause the most pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'd say like um you know, trying to touch my pinky with my thumb, that that hurts. Um just like trying to rotate it hurts.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um have you tried anything for the pain that has helped?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I haven't really tried too much. I've just I just tried not to use it as much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see. OK. And um, has this ever like, have you ever had any injuries to this hand? Any trauma either recently or in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, and is there any, do you do any kind of repetitive work that requires gripping or lifting um with that hand, anything repetitive?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I do a lot of work at the computer. And um I guess I tend to type a lot with my left hand, so maybe that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: And sorry I also take lots of notes, like handwritten notes with my left hand.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so are you left handed?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright. Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, so you're healthy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um do you take any medications on a regular basis?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. Any allergies to any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um no allergies.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um any previous surgeries or hospitalizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, any family history of any medical conditions, whether it's musculoskeletal, rheumatological, any conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um any cancers in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I know there's, yeah there's a lot of cancer in the family. There's colon cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And are they first degree relatives who had those cancers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no first degree relatives, just like aunts and uncles.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh alright, and currently are you working right now or have you had any time off work or any modified duties?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um so I'm still working online, I've just um haven't been taking notes by hand anymore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, and does that help though?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yeah it it has helped a little bit because I'm not moving my hand as much so it helps with the pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you taken any uh Tylenol, Advil, anything for the pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright. And currently right now, what is your living situation like?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I live in an apartment by myself.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um, do you currently uh smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I smoke, I used to smoke like five years ago, and I only did that for like a year or two, um and it wasn't very much. But I don't smoke anymore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's good. Um any alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I'll have like a beer on the weekend.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any recreational drugs like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I will take an edible like once a month.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um and yeah, those were just some of the questions I had um and we're just going to do a few things for examining, examining uh that area. So are you able to make a fist?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I can, but it hurts.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, it hurts in that location that you mentioned?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about um if you make a fist without your thumb, does it still hurt or is it just when you are moving the thumb?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's just when I'm moving the thumb.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And if you were able to, are you able to uh rotate your wrist?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yes, I can rotate my wrist.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Does that hurt at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um now I just want you to do this one test. It's called a Finkelstein test. OK so I want you to flex your thumb, press it up down against your palm.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And then hold your hand, sorry.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, go ahead.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, and then after you do that, um, bring your fingers above your thumb, so just cover your thumb.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Kind of like a fist, but your thumb is on the inside of your fingers.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And then bring your uh arm out.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And with your other hand, can you, from above push your wrist downwards? So your uh pinky finger is uh pointing to the pointing to the ground.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, yep.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, and did that hurt at all? Like when you, so this is just called ulnar deviation or your um of your wrist. Does that hurt at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, that is very painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: That's very painful, OK. Alright, um and then you're also having pain with gripping and, OK, so those are kind of all the things I wanted to ask. Uh it seems that you may be having something called De Quervain's tenosynovitis. Um it's caused by some repetitive motions, uh it can be due to gripping. Sometimes it happens to new mothers who are lifting their children as well as daycare workers. It can also happen in other work environments, and so what we will first just need to do um is mainly to rule out something like osteoarthritis. You are fairly young um but if there was ever an injury in the past, it you can have early osteoarthritis in the area. So we just want to get an X-Ray. And other than that, the way we kind of deal with this issue is usually conservatively and with a splint.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And a sling for your thumb that uh helps relieve some of these symptoms, uh restricts some of your movements, reduces some of the swelling, and if it does get really bad and it's affecting your work and conservative management with pain and the splint don't work, and with physiotherapy, we do uh offer injecting corticosteroids into just right like in the area that you mentioned, right below the thumb.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um and that often has some effect as well. Um but at first, yeah, let's just do some conservative management and see if that helps. It's only been a few days, so hopefully um what we try first helps. And then we can go on from there.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK yeah, that sounds great. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Welcome, take care.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You too.
